audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer chart row 1 through Level 6 reads "Skill" while the content layer reads Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Neeko, Anivia — five rows where the page answers itself twice.
audit.why: Blooming Burst (9s at rank 1) and Tangle-Barbs (12s, 1000 range) beat Anivia's wind-up through level 5; Glacial Storm at 6 is the documented flip, and the packet chart agrees with the content layer.
Lost Chapter, level 6 Glacial Storm, Seraph's/RoA is the right ladder. Neeko's own spike is Pop Blossom at 6 — 120s at rank 1, and its wind-up is hidden while she is disguised.
audit.corrected: Stated the 120s number so the post-R window is usable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The advice says to sidestep Tangle-Barbs "behind minions". Riot's text says the tangle roots everything it passes through and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion — minions make it worse, not safer. Tangle-Barbs is also not a "sidestep tool", and no line states that Crystallize is terrain against a 600-range Pop Blossom leap.
audit.why: Point 4 is the whole matchup here: standing behind the wave is the single most common way an Anivia eats an empowered root, and the empowered root is what makes Pop Blossom land.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the root advice to sidestep laterally in open ground, and named the wall-versus-leap interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues anywhere in this matchup.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs is 12s at rank 1 and Blooming Burst 9s; without those numbers "step up on its downtime" is unusable.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, phases[1].why and dosFull[0].d.

notes: Neeko is female; tldr, winCon, phases[0-2].why and multiple report entries used "he/his" — corrected where edited. Substantive fix: the existing text told the player to dodge Tangle-Barbs behind minions, but Riot's text says the tangle roots everything it passes through and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting when it kills an enemy or passes a champion, so the wave makes it worse. The packet flags zero sequencing cues for this matchup; I supplied the 12s / 9s / 120s numbers. I did not assert whether Flash Frost's stun interrupts Pop Blossom's preparation — the kit file does not flag R as a channel and I could not verify it.
